title: Enterprise Usage Variance Allocator & Invoice Timing Guideline
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This guideline explains how Redwood allocates usage variance between hosted and committed billing tiers, aligns invoice timing to revenue recognition rules, and ties procurement/contract triggers to forecast reconciliation. It is intended for finance, customer success, sales, and procurement teams supporting enterprise and Dedicated customers.

Scope:
- Applies to revenue and billing events for: Redwood Hosted API (on-demand usage), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Dedicated burst/overage events.
- Covers monthly and quarterly forecasting, invoice timing, standard credit/acceleration mechanisms, and GL mapping for RevRec and billing.
- Excludes: Marketplace partner resells, one-off professional services which are covered in separate PS billing SOPs.

Definitions:
- Baseline Commit: customer’s contracted monthly committed capacity (tokens/seat-hours) for Dedicated or committed-hosted tiers.
- Usage Variance: (Actual usage - Baseline Commit) / Baseline Commit, expressed as percent.
- Acceleration: contractual right to invoice a customer earlier than standard invoice cadence due to sustained over-commitment.
- Smoothing Credit: credit applied when average usage < 70% of commit for a contiguous quarter.

Policy overview (high level):
- Monthly reconciliation window: close on business day 7 of the next month. Finance publishes reconciled usage by day 9.
- Invoice timing: standard invoices generated on day 10 for the prior month; exceptions below trigger adjusted invoice timing or one-off adjustments.
- Variance thresholds that change behavior:
  - Low variance (±12%): auto-reconciled, billed on standard cadence.
  - Moderate overage (12% < variance ≤ 40%): billed as overage on next invoice; Sales notified for potential commit increase.
  - High overage (variance > 40% for two consecutive months OR > 100% in a single month): triggers the Contract Acceleration Checklist and potential immediate invoice of estimated run-rate for the remainder of the term.
  - Underutilization (average usage < 70% for a rolling 90-day window): triggers Smoothing Credit review; customer success & sales to propose commit re-negotiation.

Allocation & reconciliation algorithm (operational):
1) Data ingestion: daily usage events are exported from the Usage Pipeline (service: usage-collector) into the finance-reconcile bucket in Parquet.
2) Aggregate window: compute monthly token-hours per customer with the SQL below (example):
   SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', event_time) AS month, SUM(token_count) AS tokens_month
   FROM usage_events
   WHERE customer_id = '<CUSTOMER_ID>'
   GROUP BY 1,2;
3) Baseline lookup: join tokens_month to contract_table.commit_tokens for the month.
4) Compute variance and apply thresholds.
5) Produce adjustment lines: overage_line = max(0, tokens_month - commit_tokens) * overage_rate; underutil_credit = if avg_rolling_90 < 0.7 * commit_tokens then compute smoothing credit per contract.

Thresholds and notification rules (examples):
- Automated alerts: PagerDuty (finance-usage-alert) if any customer hits > 60% month-over-month increase or variance > +100% in any month.
- Email digest: weekly variance summary to Sales Ops and CS leadership for accounts with variance in the 12–40% band.
- SLA impact: for Dedicated customers with 95th percentile token-latency SLOs impacted due to sustained overage, escalate to Platform Ops to consider burst allocation.

Invoice timing & RevRec alignment:
- Standard case (on-demand or small overage): invoice = monthly, recognized as usage revenue (line: hosted_usage) in the month the usage occurred.
- Committed capacity: invoiced monthly or monthly pro-rated portion of annual commit per contract; revenue recognized ratably over the committed service period unless contract states performance obligations differ.
- Acceleration case: when Contract Acceleration fires (see triggers above), Finance issues a pro-forma invoice for the estimated incremental commit for the remainder of the term. This is recognized as deferred revenue and amortized over the remaining service period, unless there is clear evidence of deliverable completion per ASC 606.
- Example scenarios:
  - Customer A (Monthly commit 100M tokens): actual 150M tokens in May. Variance = +50%. Single-month > 40% so: May invoice will include 50M tokens at overage rate. If June again > 40%, contract acceleration kicks in and Sales Operations will receive a recommended commit increase for an amendment.
  - Customer B (Annual prepay for Dedicated): prepay covers 12 months. If usage exceeds prepay allocation by >20% three months in a row, Finance will raise an overage invoice and Sales is tasked to engage for an amendment.

Procurement & contract trigger alignment:
- When forecasted committed capacity increases by more than 25% vs last-quarter forecast, Procurement must:
  1) Validate hardware/GPU capacity (eng-infra) availability.
  2) Confirm revised pricing tiers with Legal and Sales Ops.
  3) Prepare contract amendment template (contract-ops/amendment-v2).
- Contract amendment process (condensed):
  1) Sales requests amendment via CRM and tags finance-legal.
 2) Finance produces estimated MRC/ARR impact, Procurement confirms supplier capacity if Dedicated on-prem dependencies exist.
  3) Legal reviews contract language and escrow/KMS conditions if data residency impacted.
  4) Signatures and amendment effective date are recorded; accounting posts adjustment and updates the contract_table.

Approval matrix (simplified):
- Commit delta <= 25% and delta ARR <= $100k: Sales Lead approval + Finance notification.
- Commit delta > 25% or delta ARR > $100k: Sales Director + Finance Partner + Legal review.
- Commit delta > 100% or delta ARR > $1M: VP Sales + Head of Finance + Legal + Procurement capacity sign-off.

GL mapping and sample lines (table format explained in text):
- GL mappings (use these ledger keys for downstream reporting):
  - hosted_usage -> Revenue:4000
  - committed_capacity_monthly -> Revenue:4100
  - committed_capacity_prepaid -> DeferredRevenue:2300
  - overage_charges -> Revenue:4200
  - smoothing_credits -> ContraRevenue:8000
- Sample journal for an overage month:
  - Debit Accounts Receivable (AR:1200) = $25,000
  - Credit Revenue:4200 (overage) = $25,000

Operational runbook: month-end reconciliation (steps):
1) Day 1-3: usage pipeline validation — run data integrity queries against usage-collector daily exports.
2) Day 4-6: compute monthly aggregates and preliminary variances; generate draft adjustment lines and attach supporting query results.
3) Day 7: Finance posts reconciliation and opens review thread.
4) Day 8: Notify Sales/CS for any accounts with variance > 12%.
5) Day 9: Finalize invoice-ready adjustments. Day 10: billing system (invoicing-service) issues invoices.
6) Day 11–15: monitor for disputes; Customer Success must respond to initial queries within 72 hours.

Automated scripts & example SQL snippets (operational):
- Quick check for >40% overage:
  SELECT customer_id, month, tokens_month, commit_tokens, (tokens_month::float / commit_tokens) - 1 AS variance_pct
  FROM monthly_usage JOIN contract_table USING (customer_id, month)
  WHERE ((tokens_month::float / commit_tokens) - 1) > 0.4;
- Monthly smoothing credit compute (example pseudo-SQL):
  WITH rolling AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(tokens_month) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_3mo, commit_tokens FROM monthly_usage JOIN contract_table USING (customer_id))
  SELECT customer_id, avg_3mo, commit_tokens, CASE WHEN avg_3mo < 0.7 * commit_tokens THEN (commit_tokens - avg_3mo) * smoothing_rate ELSE 0 END AS smoothing_credit FROM rolling;

Escalation & ownership:
- Finance (monthly reconciliation): Maya Chen (finance partner) — primary owner.
- Sales Ops: Priya Nair — notification & amendment execution lead.
- Procurement: Diego Alvarez — capacity & supplier confirmation for Dedicated/on-prem.
- Legal: Ethan Brooks — contract language, acceleration clauses, and data residency review.
- Platform Ops: On-call runbook for Dedicated burst capacity (see eng-platform/runbooks).

Audit & controls:
- Every adjusted invoice must include: data export link, SQL checksum hash, contract snapshot (version id), and approver signature (Sales leader).
- Random sampling: quarterly internal audit will sample 10% of adjusted invoices for supporting evidence and GL mapping.

Change history:
